observation.visible_scene: Two transparent plastic cups stand side by side against a dark backdrop with a soft, blurry orange-red glow centered between them. Each cup has a vertical green paper strip fixed to its front face, and each strip carries a short horizontal dark ink mark at roughly the same height. The left cup contains a clear liquid (filled to about the level of the ink mark on its left side) and a crinkled transparent plastic liner. The right cup contains a clear liquid (surface below the ink mark) and a transparent plastic liner holding two oval, mottled green-brown fruit pieces, with additional crinkled plastic/ice-like material near the rim.
visible_changes: Across the whole excerpt the cups, green strips, ink marks, liquid surfaces, and the two fruit pieces remain at the same positions; comparing the first and last frames shows no measurable translation, expansion, or deformation of these elements.
The background orange glow and the cup outlines stay fixed, indicating no camera pan, tilt, or zoom.
Only negligible, frame-to-frame shimmer/refraction variations are visible within the transparent plastic liners and the liquid; no object moves through the scene.
The interval is effectively static: no onset, contact, migration of the ink, or completion of any action is observed within the cropped segment.
outside_clip_unknowns: Whether the dark marks are chromatography origin lines and whether any solvent front or pigment migration is expected to occur over a longer time.
What caused or preceded the setup, and what (if anything) happens after the segment ends.
The exact materials of the liners, the fruit, and the strips.
uncertain_details: Minor apparent shifts in the crinkled plastic near the top of the right cup may be optical refraction rather than physical motion.
The precise identity of the oval objects (kiwi-like fruit vs. something else) cannot be confirmed from the frames alone.
Whether the green strips are taped to the outside or inserted into the liquid is not fully resolvable from these views.
